title: Execution Stability Certification Protocol
author: Sofia Patel
content:
Overview

This document specifies the Execution Stability Certification Protocol (ESCP): a repeatable, automated acceptance process that a runtime feature or kernel rollout must pass before being enabled for canary or production traffic. The goal is to provide deterministic gates for latency, error-rate, resource-safety, and downgrade behaviour across model variants and quantization profiles.

Goals

- Provide a short, reproducible certification path for runtime features and kernel variants.
- Ensure rollouts preserve customer-facing SLOs and do not materially increase operator toil.
- Capture behavioural contracts for fallbacks, KV cache consistency, and preemption semantics.

Scope

- Applies to: kernel releases, scheduler policy changes, KV cache algorithm changes, preemption/hothand-off logic, quantization rollout candidates.
- Excludes: experimental lab-only kernels flagged "sandbox" (see Appendix C for sandbox tagging conventions).

Acceptance criteria (table)

| Class | Metric | Gate | Measurement window |
|-------|--------|------|--------------------|
| Latency | runtime.request_latency.p95 | <= 2x baseline or absolute 1200ms (whichever lower) | 1h steady-state under canonical load |
| Error rate | runtime.request_error_rate | <= baseline + 0.1% absolute | 1h |
| Kernel stalls | kernel.hang_count | 0 detected events per 24h projected | measured during stress and 1h soak |
| KV cache correctness | kvcache.consistency_failures | 0 | end-to-end replay with golden trace |
| Resource safety | gpu.memory_exceed_events | 0 | stress profiling run |
| Degradation fidelity | degrade.fidelity_drop | no more than 5% of requests fall to lower fidelity erroneously | 2h soak |

Certification stages (high level)

1. Pre-cert: unit and integration tests; smoke benchmark on microbenchmark suite.
2. Local soak: run on single-node lab with synthetic traffic matching target cohort (sequence length distribution, token mix). Validate p50/p95 and basic telemetry.
3. Stress test: fault-injection and resource-constrained runs (OOM, NVLink flakiness, network jitter). Run soak >= 2h and track kernel stall signals.
4. Shadow canary: mirror 1–5% production traffic (no write-path) for 24h; compare divergence metrics.
5. Canary rollout: progressive, 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on gating violations.

Test harness and commands

- Harness: runtime-certify (internal test harness). Key flags:
  - --trace-corpus <path>   (replay corpus of real requests)
  - --kernel-variant <name>
  - --model-profile <json>
  - --soak-duration <minutes>
  - --stress-injector (enable fault injection)

Example run:

$ runtime-certify --trace-corpus traces/q2-webchat-8k.json --kernel-variant maelstrom-v2 --model-profile profiles/longform-8k.json --soak-duration 120 --stress-injector

YAML model-profile example (canonical subset):

model_profile:
  name: longform-8k
  avg_sequence_length: "3700"
  spike_percentile_95: "7800"
  concurrency_shape: "poisson"
  kvcache_enabled: "true"

Observability gating (signals to stream to gating engine)

- Latency: runtime.request_latency.{p50,p95,p99}
- Error: runtime.request_error_rate
- Kernel: kernel.queue_depth, kernel.active_waves, kernel.hang_count
- Memory: gpu.memory_usage_pct, gpu.vram_alloc_failures
- KV cache: kvcache.hits, kvcache.misses, kvcache.consistency_failures
- Fidelity: degrade.fidelity_drop, degrade.unexpected_falls

Gating thresholds are codified in the certification engine. Any threshold exceedance triggers an automated abort and alerts on-call.

Rollback and mitigation checklist

1. Immediately route traffic away using tiered-fallback routing to fallback-kernel (configured in routing manifest).
2. If stall pattern observed, trigger kernel-snapshot and collect live-traces: /ops/tools/collect-kernel-snapshot --target <node>
3. If KV inconsistency detected, snapshot replicas, pause rollouts, and engage DB team for trace reconciliation.
4. For memory pressure, disable the variant and escalate to infra; append nodes to dedicated-gpu-pool for burst capacity.

Rollout checklist (pre-canary)

- [ ] Automated tests green for kernel and scheduler policy
- [ ] Benchmark harness: 90th percentile runtime against baseline measured and stored in bench-db
- [ ] Telemetry mappings reviewed and mapped to gating engine
- [ ] Runbook updated with new signal names and escalation steps
- [ ] Reviewers signoff

Operational runbook excerpt (for oncall)

1. Observe: check runtime.request_latency.p95 and kernel.hang_count; if either spikes beyond gate, mark deployment paused.
2. Collect: runtime-certify --collect-trace --deployment <id>
3. Mitigate: enable fallback route, reduce concurrency admission using admission-controller set --target-concurrency <n>
4. Escalate: if KV failures present, page storage@redwood-inference with tag "kv-inconsistency" and attach trace id.

Appendix A — Example benchmark scenario (table)

| Scenario | Concurrency | Avg seq len | Warm cache | Ramp |
|---------|-------------:|------------:|-----------:|-----|
| baseline | 50 | 300 | yes | 10m |
| peak-test | 200 | 2,500 | mixed | 30m |

Appendix B — Known pitfalls and mitigations

- Non-deterministic quantized kernels: ensure bitwise-compatibility tests run for 1000 traces; if divergence > 0.2% fail.
- NVLink transient throttling: include network jitter injector in stress tests; add compensating retry logic in dispatcher.
- Replay corpus bias: rotate corpora monthly and sample by traffic cohorts to avoid overfitting to a single client pattern.

Appendix C — Tagging and metadata for sandbox kernels

- sandbox:true (disallowed for certification) 
- stability_level: experimental|beta|stable
- required_metadata: changelist-id, kernel-binary-hash, compatible-model-ids
